=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .github/workflows/implement.yml:1892-1894 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The approved-deletions regex does not tolerate CRLF line endings, so the one-shot bulk-delete override can be skipped.
  WHY: A CRLF comment body can make extraction fail and leave the issue stuck at the bulk-delete threshold.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:182-189 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash]
  PROBLEM: Failure to post a fix-up wait marker logs an error but does not set `ops_failed`.
  WHY: The verdict is recorded as acted without a parent marker, allowing a later scan to create duplicate fix-up issues.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:478-479 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The project-binding check omits `validation_active_fix_issues`, so an issue tracked only there is rejected as an unverified project member.
  WHY: The failed membership check causes the judge to return without acting on the verdict.
- scripts/unblock_actions.py:221-238 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: For a `blocked` stop, `auto_answer` posts `/answer` without transitioning the item into a phase where the clarify workflow processes it.
  WHY: The item remains `ai:blocked`, so the posted answer is dropped and the verdict has no effect.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:487-494 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: Two `last` jq filters lack an empty-string fallback for empty or whitespace-only comment bodies.
  WHY: `last` returns `null`, causing the downstream string checks to miss markers that should be copied and leaving a project-ledger hole.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:563-578 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: When actuation and the project-record write both fail, the function returns before logging the actuation failure.
  WHY: Workflow logs show only the project-record failure, concealing that the verdict also failed to carry out.
- scripts/unblock_actions.py:144-152 | severity=low | confidence=1
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: No current defect was identified: the PR reset dispatches review before removing the label.
  WHY: This ordering leaves the label for retry when dispatch fails and is described as implementing the documented contract.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:554-616 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Project activation verification runs inline in the poller, outside the shared `operator-step-writer` concurrency group used by other tracker writers.
  WHY: Concurrent read-modify-write operations can overwrite tracker updates or create duplicate `ai:operator-step` issues.
- .github/workflows/issue_pr_status.yml:728-735 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: All merged-PR activation verifiers share one concurrency group, where a later run can replace an earlier pending run.
  WHY: The replaced PR receives no activation verdict or follow-up, and the project-completion check does not recover the missing PR-mode check.
- tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py:950-1005 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash]
  PROBLEM: The template-mirror parity test fails because `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py` differs from its workflow-template mirror.
  WHY: The mismatch fails the required CI check and skips subsequent test steps in that job.
- .github/workflows/ci.yml:457-460 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The supplied run reports five failed tests in `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator`, and the failure remains unresolved.
  WHY: The test command exits nonzero, stopping the job before the new activation and unblock test steps and causing aggregate `lint` to fail.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:1990-2003, 23317-23321 | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The workflow passes `JUDGE_OUTPUT_FAILURE_MAX` through without validating it, while the poller uses it in integer comparisons.
  WHY: A non-integer repository variable can make the comparison fail under `set -euo pipefail` and stop subsequent project ticks.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: The `capture` expressions in the fixup-request parser and the wait-marker parser carry `?` so a non-matching first line returns `null` instead of failing the whole `jq` pass.
  expected_change_site: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:15772 and scripts/unblock_judge.sh:103
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  EVIDENCE: `orchestrate_poll_process.sh:15772` still reads `capture("^<!-- ai:unblock-fixup-request:v1 item=...-->$") as $m` without `?`; `unblock_judge.sh:103` reads `capture("^<!-- ai:unblock-wait:v1 item=...-->$") as $m` without `?`; the evidence also identifies the missing `validation_active_fix_issues` binding check, empty-comment-body `// ""` guards, and actuation-failure log placement.
- requirement: "Tests — New: tests/test_unblock_judge.py (56) and tests/test_unblock_scan.py (14). … The affected-test sweep: 138 test files, 3524 passed. The one failure, tests/test_audit_plans_command.py::test_template_parity, fails identically on main."
  expected_change_site: `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py` test_audit_plans_command expectation, and the activation-verify/unblock-judge ci.yml steps at lines 487-502.
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: the supplied CI run reports "5 failed, 171 passed in 5.49s" in `tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py`, upstream of the PR's newly added activation-verify and unblock-judge ci.yml steps; the reported failing test file does not match the PR description's stated failure.
- requirement: "Activation-verifier and unblock-judge jobs share the repository-scoped `operator-step-writer-<repo>` concurrency group so their tracker read-modify-writes cannot race. The scan dispatches at most one judge when no judge is active to avoid GitHub replacing a pending run in that group."
  expected_change_site: `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` invocation site of `scripts/activation_verify.sh project` (around line 600-608) and the `run_unblock_scan` call site.
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: `run_project_activation_verify` and `run_unblock_scan` execute inline in the poller and lack the shared concurrency declaration; `orchestrate_poll.yml`'s poll job carries no `concurrency: operator-step-writer-...` group; only `issue_pr_status.yml`'s `activation-verify` and `unblock_judge.yml`'s `unblock-judge` jobs declare the shared group.
- requirement: "Operator steps only you can take arrive in the `ai:operator-step` issue, with the work kept off behind a flag until you act."
  expected_change_site: the `operator_step` verdict's `placeholder` enforcement in the consuming code, plus the activation verifier's "code" gaps that should reference an `_ENABLED` flag or `_UNSET_OPERATOR_STEP` placeholder.
  confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: `scripts/unblock_ledger.py:344-359` checks only that `placeholder` is syntactically valid and ends in `_ENABLED` or `_UNSET_OPERATOR_STEP`; `scripts/unblock_actions.py:243-248` passes that name through; the evidence reports no producer or consumer verifies that the named gate exists in code.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:478-479 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The project-binding check against V2 state enumerates `issue_number_map`, `waves[].issues[]`, and `security_pass_active_fix_issues`, but does NOT check `validation_active_fix_issues`. A managed issue that is only tracked in that field (e.g. a validation fix-up) would be rejected as an unverified project member, causing the judge to skip actuation.
  WHY: `orchestrate_state_v2.py extract` returns the full state; the jq filter asserts membership in lists that do not include `validation_active_fix_issues`. A validation fix-up present only there fails the `jq -e` test, logs `project_binding_unverified`, and returns without acting on the verdict. The LAST RUN DIFF documents this gap was known and a fix was authored, but the fix is not present on disk.
- scripts/unblock_actions.py:221-237 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The `auto_answer` verdict path only transitions to the clarification phase when `ctx["stop"] == "needs-human"` and `"ai:needs-human"` in labels. For any other stop (including plain `"blocked"`), the item keeps its block label and `/answer` is posted without entering `ai:clarification`. The clarify workflow processes `/answer` only for items carrying `ai:clarification` or `ai:planning`, so a blocked item's auto-answer may not be acted on by any workflow.
  WHY: The `auto_answer` verdict fires for a `blocked`-labeled issue; the code never calls `add_labels` with `ai:clarification`; `/answer` is posted but the clarify workflow's comment handler skips it because the issue is not in the clarification or planning phase. The verdict is recorded as acted but had no effect.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:487-494 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Two `last` jq filters on comment-body line arrays lack a `// ""` fallback. When a comment body is empty or whitespace-only, the array `[lines]` is empty, `last` produces `null`, and the downstream `startswith` and `contains` string operations on `null` silently produce `false`, causing the ledger-repair scan to miss markers that should be copied.
  WHY: An item verdict comment on an item whose project copy failed to post goes undetected when an intervening comment body is empty. The marker reconciliation loop finds no missing markers and the project-ledger hole remains, allowing a future verdict repeat (the ledger counts rounds from both copies).
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:563-578 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: When both actuation AND the project-record write fail, the code returns at line 572 before reaching the actuation failure log at line 575-577. The actuation failure is never logged for this combined-failure case. The LAST RUN DIFF shows an attempted fix (moving the log to line 566, before the project-record block) but that fix is not on disk.
  WHY: Both failures together produce only the `op=project_record outcome=failed` log line, making the actuation failure invisible in workflow logs. Operators and the workflow-log analysis pipeline see the project mark fail but not that the verdict itself also failed to carry out, which can mask follow-up errors.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:554-616 (run_project_activation_verify) and .github/workflows/issue_pr_status.yml:716-849 (activation-verify job) and .github/workflows/unblock_judge.yml:30-39 (unblock-judge concurrency group) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The poller's `run_project_activation_verify` runs `scripts/activation_verify.sh project` inline within the poller process, not as a dispatched workflow job. It therefore does NOT participate in the `operator-step-writer-<repo>` concurrency group that serializes the `issue_pr_status.yml` activation-verify job and the `unblock_judge.yml` unblock-judge job. Both the inline activation verify and either workflow job can call `operator_step_issue.py upsert` concurrently, performing a read-modify-write on the single `ai:operator-step` issue body.
  WHY: A project completes and the poller runs `run_project_activation_verify` while an unblock judge is simultaneously dispatching. Both read the issue body, both compute a modified body, both PATCH. The first writer's changes are silently over
